patch_description: Combines the two most successful prior ideas: (1) a single shared scalar parameter "theta" driving three non-commuting single-qubit rotation axes (RX → RY → RZ) sandwiching the entangling layer, which gave fast convergence (convergence_step_mean 60) in an earlier generation, and (2) the richer dual-ring entangling topology (nearest-neighbor CZ ring plus skip-2 CZ ring) from the most recent generation, which gave very low validation/test loss but suffered slow convergence (240 steps) because it lacked the RX pre-rotation axis. By reusing the same single parameter name across all three rotation layers (RX, RY, RZ) we keep the per-block parameter count minimal (still just 1 unique trainable scalar per block repetition, i.e. n_params stays at the same economical level as before) while restoring the fast-convergence benefit of spanning three rotation axes and retaining the expressive dual-ring entanglement. The expectation is to match or exceed the 1.00 train/val accuracy and low loss of the current program while cutting convergence_step_mean back down toward ~60, improving the overall combined score (which rewards parameter economy, low gap, and fast convergence).
